title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
technique: (a) observation masking of old tool outputs (window M=10) vs (b) LLM summarization of old turns (N=21 summarized, M=10 kept); SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified, n=500 per model, 5 model configs
measured_saving: Cost per instance down 50.9% to 57.1% for observation masking across 5 configs (Qwen3-32B -50.9%, Qwen3-Coder-480B -52.7%, Gemini 2.5 Flash -56.1%); LLM summarization down 41.5% to 55.4%. Summary API overhead 0.65% to 7.2% of cost. Qwen3-Coder: masking $0.676 vs summary $0.649 saved per instance (about $0.03 apart).
quality_effect: Solve rate change vs raw: masking -11.8% (Qwen3-32B) to +8.5% (Gemini Flash); summarization -5.9% to +9.8%. Only significant drops: Gemini Flash thinking, masking -4.0pp (p=0.041), summary -9.0pp (p<0.001). Hybrid (masking early, summary at N=43) on Qwen3-Coder-480B, 50 instances: +2.6pp vs raw, 7% cheaper than masking, 11% cheaper than summary. OpenHands transfer needed a retuned window.
applies_to_us: High. Directly answers (a): clearing old tool outputs matches summarization at about half the cost with no summarizer call. Caveats: SWE-bench only, fixed heuristic windows, hybrid tested on 50 instances and one model. Use a window of about 10 turns as the starting point, then measure on our own runs.

title: ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
technique: Learned natural-language compression guidelines for both interaction history and environment observations, refined from paired trajectories where full context succeeds but compressed context fails; optional distillation into small compressors (ICML 2026)
measured_saving: Peak token usage down 26% to 54% across AppWorld, OfficeBench, and 8-objective QA (QA peak -54.5%, dependency -61.5%). AppWorld API cost per task $0.331 to $0.285 (history) or $0.272 (observation), about -14% to -18%. Distilled Qwen3-14B compressor costs $0.0004 per example vs $0.045 for gpt-4.1 (-99.1%). Wall-clock latency rises (73s to 88-102s).
quality_effect: AppWorld 56.0 to 56.5 accuracy (history); OfficeBench 76.84 to 74.74 (history, -2.1 pts) and 72.63 (observation); QA EM 0.366 to 0.373. Distilled compressors keep over 95% of teacher performance. Small agent Qwen3-14B AppWorld 25.6% to 33.9%.
applies_to_us: Medium. The method needs an optimizer loop and a compressor LLM call per step, so it is heavier than our native compaction. Useful as a design source for what a compaction prompt must keep (recall first, then precision), and for distilling a cheap summarizer. OfficeBench result shows precise-fact tasks lose accuracy under history compression.

title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding
technique: Branch/return sub-trajectories: a subtask runs in a temporary branch and collapses to a short summary on return; trained end-to-end with FoldGRPO (process rewards)
measured_saving: Authors report active context about 10x smaller than ReAct on Deep Research and SWE tasks; main trajectory about 8K tokens while processing over 100K total (over 90% compression).
quality_effect: Authors report matching or beating ReAct and summarization-based context management. Ablation vs plain GRPO: SWE-Bench Verified finish rate 0.612 to 0.962; BrowseComp-Plus finish 0.738 to 0.935. Self-reported; no independent replication found.
applies_to_us: Low-to-medium. The branch/return pattern is the same idea as delegating a reading task to a sub-agent that returns a short summary, which we can do now with Claude Code sub-agents. The RL training part does not apply to us.

title: Context management (context editing and memory tool)
technique: (a) Context editing: automatically clears stale tool calls and results when approaching token limits; (b) memory tool stored client-side outside the window
measured_saving: Token consumption down 84% in a 100-turn web-search evaluation (context editing enabled); the same eval had workflows that otherwise failed from context exhaustion. No baseline, task design, or trigger threshold given.
quality_effect: Context editing alone +29% on an internal agentic-search eval; memory tool plus context editing +39% over baseline. Vendor-reported, public beta.
applies_to_us: High. This is the native mechanism for clearing old tool outputs that our harness can rely on. The threshold is unspecified, so measure our own trigger point with the usage instruments before tuning it.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
technique: Orchestrator (Opus 4) with parallel sub-agents (Sonnet 4) that each return condensed findings; compared against a single Opus 4 agent
measured_saving: Agents use about 4x chat tokens; multi-agent systems about 15x chat tokens. Token usage alone explains 80% of variance in BrowseComp performance.
quality_effect: Multi-agent scored 90.2% higher than single-agent Opus 4 on Anthropic's internal research eval.
applies_to_us: High for (c). Sub-agents cost tokens in total (about 15x) but keep the main context small, so delegating reading is worth it only when the task value justifies the spend. Our Haiku scout/librarian/researcher pattern fits this cost profile.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
technique: Compaction (summarize near the limit), tool result clearing (the lightest form), and sub-agents returning condensed summaries
measured_saving: No numbers for compaction or clearing. Sub-agents may use tens of thousands of tokens and return condensed summaries of about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens.
quality_effect: No quantitative results. Warns that overly aggressive compaction can lose subtle but critical context; advises maximizing recall first.
applies_to_us: Medium. Gives the design rule (clear tool results first, compact last, sub-agents return 1-2K tokens) but no threshold. Our compaction trigger has to come from our own measurements.

title: Multi-Agents: What's Actually Working
technique: Single-threaded writes with read-only or review sub-agents; share full context; clean-context review of diffs (follow-up to the 2025 Don't Build Multi-Agents post)
measured_saving: None reported. Cost described only qualitatively.
quality_effect: Parallel writers make conflicting implicit choices and produce fragile products; the review agent with a clean context avoids noise from a long session. Devin Review finds about 2 bugs per PR, 58% severe (their figure).
applies_to_us: High for (c) as a constraint: let sub-agents read, search and review, but keep writes in one thread. Not a cost measurement.

title: Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents in Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
technique: 8 condensers in OpenHands CodeActAgent: 5 heuristic (observation masking, recent events, conversation window, amortized forgetting, NoOp) and 3 LLM-based (LLM summarizing, structured summary, LLM attention); thresholds max_size=8, keep_first=2
measured_saving: Tokens per task vs NoOp (75,147 baseline): observation masking 68,718 (-8.6% tokens, saved); conversation window -1.2%; LLM summarizing 92,880 (+23.6% tokens, costs more); structured summary +59%; LLM attention +93.9%. Short tasks (7 events or fewer) had overhead for all condensers.
quality_effect: Heuristic condensers 100% task completion; LLM condensers 93-98%. Hypothesis quality: NoOp 0.591, observation masking 0.572, LLM summarizing 0.637; no significant difference (Wilcoxon, Bonferroni, p>0.05). Sign convention of the tasks-over-10-events column (observation masking +33.5%) is unclear in the extract.
applies_to_us: Medium. Important caveat for us: on this benchmark, LLM condensers raised token use, so summarization is not a free saving. Only one backbone (GPT-4o), 60 tasks, short 5-22 event runs; does not cover our long multi-hour runs. Use it as a warning against summarization-first.

title: Context condensation for more efficient AI agents (OpenHands blog)
technique: LLMSummarizingCondenser: summarize older events once context reaches a size threshold
measured_saving: Headline up to 2x per-turn API cost reduction; body says average per-turn cost is less than half of baseline. Exact figures only in charts.
quality_effect: Solve rate about 54% with condenser vs 53% baseline on a SWE-bench Verified subset; model and instance count not stated. Turn counts sometimes rise because condensing takes an extra turn.
applies_to_us: Low-to-medium. Vendor-reported with missing methodology; the 1-point solve-rate gap is within noise. Treat the 2x claim as an upper bound.

title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
technique: KV-cache-stable prefix (append-only context, deterministic serialization); restorable compression to the sandbox file system; logit masking of tools instead of removing them; todo.md recitation
measured_saving: No measured percent in the post. Cached input priced $0.30/MTok vs $3/MTok uncached (Sonnet), about 10x; average input-to-output token ratio about 100:1.
quality_effect: Qualitative only. A single-token prefix change invalidates the cache from that point; tool add/remove mid-iteration breaks the cache and confuses the model. Typical task about 50 tool calls.
applies_to_us: High for (a) and cache economics. Keep dynamic content (timestamps, state) out of the top of the system prompt and CLAUDE.md, and keep tool-output clearing as a reference (path or URL) rather than deletion, so a cleared result can be re-read.
